name: Kinso
tagline: An AI assistant product at kinso.ai; the exact scope is not confirmed at draft time.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Honest disclosure first: we have not verified what Kinso actually does, so treat this page as a stub rather than a ruling. What we can say is structural: a small AI product on a .ai domain, with no obvious network of users and no visible proprietary corpus, is usually a prompt pipeline plus a nice interface plus billing. That shape is genuinely weekend-buildable once you bring your own model key, and the gaps are the usual ones: no mobile app, no hosted sync, no integrations you did not write yourself. If Kinso turns out to sit on top of private data, a real integration graph, or a regulated workflow, this verdict should move to no. Until someone checks, the consolation build below gives you the generic version of the category.
coreLoopDIY: Runs a local web app where you chat with a model over your own notes and files, with saved prompts for the tasks you repeat.
requirements: An API key for an OpenAI-compatible model
Node 20 and a machine you are willing to leave running
Willingness to paste your own data in, since there is no importer
whatYouLose: Whatever specific workflow Kinso has actually tuned, which we have not verified
A mobile app and cross device sync
Prebuilt integrations with the tools you already use
Someone else's problem when the model provider changes behaviour or pricing
Support, onboarding, and a team that iterates on the thing while you sleep
moatNotes: Thin moats by default for products in this shape, but unconfirmed: if there is a real data or integration layer under the marketing, the picture changes.
whyPeopleStillPay: People pay for AI assistants because the value is in the last ten percent: the defaults that stop you thinking, the phone app that works on the train, the account that survives your laptop dying. A local build gets you the loop, not the habit. If Kinso has done that ten percent well, a subscription is cheaper than your weekend.

prompt:
Build a local, single user AI assistant web app in an empty folder. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non negotiable:
- Next.js 15 with the App Router and TypeScript
- Tailwind CSS for styling, no component library
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/app.db, migrations in plain SQL on boot
- Model calls through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint using OPENAI_API_KEY and OPENAI_BASE_URL from .env.local, never hardcoded

Features in scope:
1. Chat page with streaming responses, conversation list in a sidebar, all messages persisted in SQLite.
2. A Library page where I paste text snippets or upload .txt and .md files. Store the raw text, chunk it at roughly 800 tokens, embed chunks with the embeddings endpoint, keep vectors in SQLite as JSON blobs.
3. Retrieval: on each chat turn, cosine similarity in plain TypeScript over stored vectors, inject the top 6 chunks into the system prompt with their source titles. Brute force is fine, do not add a vector database.
4. A Prompts page for saved reusable prompts with a title, body, and optional {{input}} placeholder. Running one starts a new conversation.
5. Show the source titles used for each answer under the reply.

Out of scope, do not build: authentication, multi user support, billing, mobile apps, third party integrations, background jobs, PDF parsing, Docker.

Deliverables: working app on npm run dev, an .env.example, and a README with setup steps and one honest paragraph on what this build does badly.
